reading.body:
T5 Chicago II's actual power capacity cannot be determined because the operator publishes no facility-specific figures and the facility page is no longer accessible.

T5 Data Centers operates 22 facilities totaling over 3 gigawatts nationwide, but this Chicago-area campus discloses neither capacity nor square footage. Illinois has 44 mapped data centers, yet only 6 publish power figures. The 236 megawatts of disclosed capacity in the state comes from those six facilities. T5 Chicago II's published capacity either equals zero or falls below the minimum disclosed figure statewide, placing it seventh or lower in the state by whatever power it may hold.

This creates a gap between operator scale and facility transparency. A developer managing 3-plus gigawatts across multiple states has both the capital and expertise to build substantial infrastructure, but investors and researchers cannot verify this particular site's contribution to regional compute or power demand without disclosed specifications.

The facility cannot be assessed as material to AI infrastructure scaling until the operator publishes power delivery, cooling capability, or footprint. The inaccessible facility page suggests either recent changes in the operator's web presence or that this project remains unpublished in its specifications. Illinois data center capacity remains partially invisible.
